Study exercise derived from this source. Explain the approach in your own words, work through an example, and identify edge cases. For code, implement your own version and discuss its time and space complexity.

#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
using namespace std;

int sumOfEvenIndexInReversedArray(const vector<int>& arr) {
    int sum = 0;
    int n = arr.size();

    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        int Ridx=n - 1 - i;
        if (Ridx % 2 == 0) {
            sum += arr[i];
        }
    }

    return sum;
}

int main() {
    // Example array
    vector<int> arr = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6};

    int result = sumOfEvenIndexInReversedArray(arr);
    cout << "Sum of elements at even indices in the reversed array: " << result << endl;

    return 0;
}
